operations.evidence: The statistical bulletin was released on 23 July 2026.
Release timing does not make the figures parcel-level or real-time.
The year ending March 2026 Crime Survey for England and Wales estimated 9.6 million incidents of headline crime, with no statistically significant annual change.
Survey estimates have sampling uncertainty and do not identify exact addresses.
CSEW headline crime was 14% lower than in the year ending March 2017.
The comparison begins when fraud and computer misuse were included in the headline measure.
Police recorded around 5.2 million crimes excluding fraud and computer misuse, 1% fewer than the previous year.
Recorded crime is affected by reporting, recording practice and police activity.
Police recorded 499 homicide offences, 7% fewer than the previous year.
National homicide counts cannot be assigned to a parcel without separate exact-location evidence.
The homicide rate was 8.1 per million people, down from 8.9 per million.
A national population rate is not a local or parcel risk probability.
Knife or sharp instrument homicides fell 14% to 176 offences.
Weapon-category counts are national aggregates and do not establish local exposure.
Knife-enabled crime recorded by police fell 8% to 48,774 offences.
By March 2026, 41 forces had switched to the NDQIS identification method, affecting comparability.
Assault with injury or intent accounted for 44% and robbery for 39% of knife-enabled crimes.
The shares describe offence composition, not severity or parcel-level safety.
Police recorded 5,151 offences involving firearms, 8% fewer than the previous year.
The measure excludes conventional air weapons and British Transport Police.
Imitation firearms accounted for 38% and handguns for 31% of recorded firearms offences.
Weapon-type shares do not locate incidents or identify affected properties.
People aged 16 years and over experienced an estimated 989,000 incidents of violence with or without injury, with no statistically significant annual change.
The estimate is survey-based and excludes children from the respondent population.
About 0.7% reported stranger violence and 0.4% reported acquaintance violence.
Prevalence percentages are population estimates, not exact-area indicators.
Police categorised 834,256 offences as domestic-abuse-related, including 643,061 violence-against-the-person offences.
Police data do not measure domestic-abuse prevalence and are affected by recording practices.
An estimated 2.1% of people aged 16 years and over, around 1 million people, experienced sexual victimisation including attempts.
New survey questions mean the estimate is not comparable with previously published measures.
Police recorded 217,567 sexual offences, 4% more than the previous year.
Recorded trends reflect reporting and recording changes as well as underlying incidents.
Robbery of personal property fell 9% to 57,693 offences.
Police data are preferred for robbery but remain subject to recording changes.
Overall robbery rose 10% to 87,362 offences, mainly because of improved recording of robbery of business property.
The increase should not be read as a like-for-like rise in personal robbery.
The CSEW estimated 2.6 million theft incidents, with no statistically significant annual change and 29% fewer than a decade earlier.
Survey theft covers several offence types and is not an exact property register.
Police recorded vehicle offences fell 11% to 312,250.
Recorded vehicle crime does not identify parcel exposure without local geospatial evidence.
Police recorded burglary fell 9% to 223,456 offences.
The figure combines residential and non-residential burglary.
Police recorded theft from the person fell 20% to 121,161 offences.
National change does not establish neighbourhood or parcel conditions.
Police recorded shoplifting fell 4% to 507,086 offences.
Reporting rates are known to be low and police-retailer engagement can affect recorded levels.
The CSEW estimated around 646,000 criminal-damage incidents, with no statistically significant annual change and 47% fewer than a decade earlier.
Survey uncertainty and broad offence coverage prevent exact parcel attribution.
The CSEW estimated 4.5 million fraud incidents, with no statistically significant annual change; prevalence rose to 7.8%.
Fraud is generally not a location-based parcel safety measure.
Bank and credit account fraud increased 15% to around 2.8 million incidents.
Financial fraud should not be merged into physical-area crime scores without a justified model.
The CSEW estimated 798,000 computer-misuse incidents, with no statistically significant annual change and 55% fewer than in the year ending March 2017.
Cyber incidents are not parcel-located and police-recorded cybercrime was temporarily omitted.
An estimated 40.9% experienced or witnessed anti-social behaviour, up from 35.5%.
The increase was inflated by changes to survey question wording from April 2025.
Police-recorded anti-social behaviour incidents remained similar at around 1 million.
Inspectorate findings indicate some forces need to improve identification and recording.
Police recorded crime data cover 43 territorial forces plus British Transport Police and were extracted as a snapshot on 8 June 2026.
A publication snapshot can be revised and does not provide exact incident coordinates.
The wave50_ source-id prefix is unique within this increment; all 30 source IDs are distinct.
Zero source roles were promoted to exact-address evidence, parcel risk, candidate values or business rows.
30 official-source rows and 64 completed operation rows were prepared for progress_latest.json line-by-line loading.
No runner was started, no queue was replaced, no candidate computation ran, and no business or database row was written.
